## Feasibility Status

| Dimension | Finding |
|-----------|---------|
| Effort | 1.5–2.5 day (realistic 2.0). This is **net-new cited authoring** (~80–150 `related` edges @ ~5 min/edge across harvest → resolve-check → calibrate → cite → insert), NOT F-186's byte-exact git-blob reconstruction. Cost drivers: **T002 build-start survey+harvest** (~1.5–4h, time-variable `[MANUAL-ONLY]`), **T004 author the `related` floor** (the heavy task, the per-edge curve), **T005 anti-drift citation audit** (~per-edge subset, `[MANUAL-ONLY]`). All verify tasks are sub-second test runs (suite re-verified live: `5 passed in 1.01s`). |
| Capacity | No agent >80% loaded. Two write surfaces only (`crosswalk.yaml` + `README.md`); the only concurrent-write hazard (US1 author vs US2 author, both on `crosswalk.yaml`) is **serialized by design** (T008 after T004). The W1 parallelism is read-surface only (T007 superseded *survey* ∥ US1 *authoring*). |
| Timeline | 15-task granularity fits the envelope. Per-edge cost concentrated in T002/T004/T005; remaining 12 tasks are minutes-scale edits, sub-second test runs, or deliver-time. The **floor (80 edges) lands at ~2.0 day** — exactly the realistic target. The **ceiling (150) is a hard upward stop (C4), not a target**; surplus beyond the high/medium core → headroom note, never authored (T004), so the envelope is bounded by the anti-drift quota, not by raw 150×5-min time. |
| Dependencies | All upstream deps DELIVERED (F-180, F-186, F-241). Live state confirms the authorable substrate: crosswalk **542 primary / 0 related / 0 superseded**; catalogs **cwe 53 / mitre-atlas 36 / mitre-attack 701 / owasp 60**; **5** integrity functions. External read-only deps: cwe.mitre.org, owasp.org/Top10, genai.owasp.org, `mitre-atlas/atlas-data`. The only material sequencing dep is **#185** (CWE-pool yield stability) — handled by C3 below (run-first-or-freeze-snapshot; write-sets are file-disjoint so never a merge collision). No hidden blocker. |

**Workload distribution**:
- **senior-backend-engineer** — 6 tasks (T001, T004, T008, T010, T012 + baseline): the authoring bulk (data edits + README + provenance). T004 is the single heavy task; the rest are minutes-scale. ~50–55% loaded.
- **web-researcher** — 2 tasks (T002, T007): the two harvest/survey surfaces (the time-variable `[MANUAL-ONLY]` T002 + the `[P]` superseded survey). ~25–30% loaded.
- **tester** — 3 tasks (T006, T009, T014): the three verification gates (all sub-second). ~15% loaded.
- **code-reviewer** — 3 tasks (T005, T011, T013): anti-drift audit + README self-sufficiency + diff guard. T005 is `[MANUAL-ONLY]` per-edge. ~25–30% loaded.
- **architect** — 1 task (T003): the no-migration / floor-authorization gate. ~5% loaded.

No agent exceeds 80% capacity. The `[MANUAL-ONLY]` time-variability is correctly isolated to web-researcher (T002) + code-reviewer (T005); the yield-tripwire (T003) caps T002 from becoming an open-ended sink.

### Real parallel opportunities (validated)
- **T007 [P] ∥ US1 lane (T004/T005)** — REAL. T007 is a *research/survey* surface writing to `reference-edges.yaml`; T004/T005 write/audit `crosswalk.yaml`. Disjoint surfaces, no write contention. Worth modeling.
- (No other read/write-disjoint pair in this feature — Polish is sequential.)

### Serialization (NOT parallel — by design)
- **T008 after T004** — both write `crosswalk.yaml`. The US2 *author* step cannot run concurrent with the US1 *author* step. Only the US2 *survey* (T007) parallelizes. tasks.md models this correctly.
- **T013 after T012** — T012 writes the `crosswalk.yaml` header + `CHANGELOG.md`; T013's no-migration diff guard must read the *final* diff (its allowed-file set includes `CHANGELOG.md`). Sequential, not parallel.
